say: Growing the business: bulk orders, fair pay and your 90-day plan.
This is the video for module 3 of Fashion Business Management.
Boutiques, schools, companies and other brands bring volume. They also ask for lower prices, longer payment times and firm deadlines. So you test every offer first.

say: With outright wholesale, the boutique buys your pieces and owns them. You give up part of the price, but the risk of unsold pieces is theirs.

panel.heading: Outright wholesale or consignment
right: Your cash waits on their shelf

say: With consignment, they pay you only for what sells, so your stock and cash wait on their shelf. Start new boutiques small, then move good partners to bigger outright orders.

panel.heading: Outright wholesale or consignment

say: A boutique offers Adaeze 11,000 naira each for 30 peplum tops, paid 60 days after delivery. Each top costs her 7,468 naira. The price works, with 3,532 naira profit per top.

items: Cost: is the price above your total cost?
Cash: what do you spend before you are paid?
Capacity: do the minutes fit your spare time?

say: But she must spend 188,400 naira on materials first, then wait 60 days. Cash is the problem. So she asks for a 50% deposit of 165,000 naira, and only funds 23,400 herself.

say: Scammers send fake transfer alerts and fake large orders. Confirm every deposit in your own bank or payment app before cutting, and never pay a fee to receive an order.

panel.rule: Confirm deposits in your own bank app, not from a screenshot.

say: Big contracts are where workrooms most often fail, because the owner says yes before checking minutes. A school asks for 200 pinafores. Each takes 40 minutes, so 8,000 minutes.

panel.heading: 200 school pinafores in a month
items: 200 × 40 minutes = 8,000 minutes
Only 6,020 minutes spare
Split: 150 now, 50 at the start of month 2
Or agreed overtime, a partner, or decline

say: If a piece rate is too low, workers rush and quality suffers. So build it from timed minutes.
Adaeze's target for a trained worker is 3,600 naira for an 8-hour day. Check it is never below the current national minimum wage for a month.

panel.heading: Build the rate from standard minutes
items: Choose a target day's pay: 3,600 naira
480 minutes ÷ 12 standard minutes = 40
At 75% efficiency: 30 pieces a day
3,600 ÷ 30 = 120 naira per good piece

say: Many workrooms blend the two. A fixed base keeps a worker steady in slow months, and a small bonus rewards good pieces above a target.

card.title: A base plus a quality bonus

say: The base is 60,000 naira a month.

card.title: A base plus a quality bonus

say: She makes 780 good pieces, 180 above the target of 600. At 60 naira each, her bonus is 10,800.

card.title: A base plus a quality bonus

say: So she earns 70,800 naira. A worker below target gets the base and coaching, not a deduction.
Write the pay method, hours, overtime, a cap on fabric deductions and notice period into a signed agreement.

card.title: A base plus a quality bonus

say: Each month, track on-time delivery and your defect rate. Adaeze delivered 187 of 210 on time, and her defects fell from 15% to 8%.

panel.heading: Five numbers on one page
items: On-time delivery %
Defect rate %
Capacity utilisation %
Average lead time
Margin by style

say: Add utilisation, lead time and margin by style. Read them together. Rising utilisation with rising defects usually means the team is rushing, so slow down intake.

say: To remember. Test every offer on cost, cash and capacity, and ask for a deposit that covers materials. Split or decline contracts bigger than your spare minutes. Build piece rates from standard minutes.
And hire another machinist only when the extra minutes are sold.
